title: The shooting at the resort
summary: The owner caught Eddie Hill in bed with his wife, shot her and himself, and Hill fled up the mountain and returned in worn-out shoes.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But what happened, he went out to the club and he walked in, you know, in front of the club, went around to the side, you know, where they had sleeping quarters there, and they also had a house over there where they slept, he and the old lady, you know. So he walked in over here in the club. Well, Eddie Hill was in there with his old lady.
So, when she heard him walking through there, she pulled the thing over Eddie, pulled -- you know, and Jim walked in and looked --
Oh, in bed. I see, yeah.

Jim walked on back to the car, went and got his .45 and come on back in there and she went to running and says, 'Oh, Jim, Jim, Jim, don't kill him. Don't kill him.' Well, in the meantime, Eddie had some brand new shoes he'd bought. He picked them shoes and clothes up and ran. See, the mountain goes right up, you know, and run up that mountain and so the old man was looking for Eddie and he's running all around there trying to find Eddie. He shot her.

Yes, see, she was out -- she come outside the club, see, and he shot her and he run around the club, looking for Eddie, and then he come back and shot her again. Then he pulled the pistol on himself. They couldn't find Eddie. Pulled the pistol on himself. About five minutes see, and I had already called out there, there was two or three guys that was cleaning up the place, and I called them and asked them, 'You all didn't have no trouble out there after I come in town?' They said no. About five minutes, they called me back and said, 'Man, yes, we did have some trouble, just now. Old man Jim come out and killed her and has killed himself and he's running up there trying to find Eddie.'

And then when he shot himself the second time, he fell right over her, you know. So consequently, the musicians inside, two of them cleaning up, all this commotion's going on, they was running over each other, running under the tables and everything else. So they called me and I said, 'Well, I'll be right back out.' So I come on back out. So by the time I got back out there, Eddie done come by the mountains and Eddie was crying, 'Oh,' and I looked at them shoes and they was wore out.
I said, 'Man, how did you wear out a pair of brand new shoes?'
